reason_codes.description: Nostr event id or BIP-340 signature verification failed.
The Matrix sender is not covered by the active delegation.
An event signed by a revoked epoch key was created after revoked_at.
The verifier clock is after the delegation valid_until bound.
A new room asserts a retired pre-ADR-017 room kind.
A KERI threshold is satisfied only if advisory vouches are counted.
A private broadcast post used the withdrawn NIP-59 wrapping path.
Relay rejected the write after NIP-42 AUTH, so the failure is permanent.
Encrypted payload decrypted under a key derived for the wrong Matrix room context.
A .onion host was sent to a clearnet resolver instead of Tor.
Strict mode started with egress-over-Tor disabled without explicit user choice.
MLS migration proceeded without all required ACKs.
A stale identity-room pointer was preferred over the migration pointer.
Friend-cache content was not owner-signed non-KERI content.
A Heterodyne-aware relay profile changed vanilla NIP-01 read/write behavior.
A receiver encountered an incompatible future major version.
A kind:31001 NID delegation lacked the epoch-key Schnorr sig or the NID Ed25519 nid_proof.
An Ed25519 nid_proof did not verify against the advertised NID over the pinned binding payload.
A kind:31010 node advertisement was past its expiry.
A NID revoked by the KEL was used as a delegate despite the identity document still listing it.
An org kind:31007 or post was not reachable from the delegate-threshold-approved canonical feed branch.
An org member NID add carried only one of the required member-KEL and org-admin-threshold authorizations.
A feed-index page's prev_page_hash did not match the prior page's canonical serialization.
A relay served an older NIP-51 list revision than one reachable in the repo's canonical history.
A kind:30078 DM invite was signed by a publishing key with no valid kind:31001 delegation to the persona.
A kind:30078 DM invite was signed by a device whose kind:31001 delegation is revoked.
A repo relay refused to store a kind:1060 double-ratchet message (or kind:1059 response); ratchet ciphertext MUST NOT be archived.
The config repository RID appeared on a published surface (kind:31005, kind:31010, kind:0, NIP-65, or a NIP-51 list).
A kind:4550 approval's moderator is not listed in the kind:34550 declaration resolved as-of the approval's anchor.
An epoch-key-signed Heterodyne event required to carry kel_head does not carry exactly one well-formed instance (absent, duplicate, or malformed).
The kel_head tag's decimal seq does not equal the s value of the KEL event it names once that event is resolved on the accepted KEL.
A kel_head tag appears on an event class the §3.0 matrix forbids it on (kind:31002/31003 KEL events, §5.7 DR wire events kind:1060/1059 and inner rumors, or ADR-031 breadcrumbs).
A structurally valid kel_head names an event that is not on the persona's accepted KEL; the verifier flags equivocation and surfaces it through the §13 security-warning interface.
The signing epoch key is retroactively non-authoritative at the event's created_at: an accepted compromise-declaring rotation covers created_at under effective_compromise_since - 300 seconds.

Acceptance rests on relay-only key-material state (kind:31002/31003/31001); under deny-until-repo policy the event does not take effect until repo-carried, and provisional-accept results MUST NOT be reported as final.
A prior provisional or §4.5.1-accelerator acceptance is withdrawn after convergence-gated repo reconciliation, a KEL update, or later full verification contradicts it.
A repo presented a key-material head regressing below a previously finalized canonical head without an authenticated re-anchor.
did:webs export failed: security-relevant KEL state uses a construct with no semantics-preserving canonical-KERI mapping (UNMAPPABLE_FEATURE).
did:webs export failed: a mapping exists but the target crypto suite is unavailable locally (UNSUPPORTED_CRYPTO_SUITE).
did:webs export failed: required source KEL events or attachments are unavailable (INCOMPLETE_EXPORT).
A KEL event or stream was presented in KERI10JSON/CESR on the Heterodyne wire or as storage; NIP-01 with nip01_raw is the only wire and storage format.
A derived export AID or its did:webs DID was substituted for the persona npub where the spec requires the npub; the export identity is never an alternate authoritative identity.
The claim or revocation does not satisfy its registered Comms schema.
The claim_id does not equal the lowercase SHA-256 digest of the canonical semantic body.
An issuer, subject, or proof key reference is malformed or uses an unregistered type.
The outer Nostr claim or revocation event signature is invalid.
Core/KEL validation does not establish the issuer's claimed authority at issuance time.
The claim is cryptographically valid but its issuer is outside the verifier's trust policy.
The claim issuance chain contains a repeated claim identifier.
The claim issuance chain exceeds the strict eight-edge limit.
The parent claim does not authorize the child issuer to redelegate.
A child claim widens scope, audience, resources, validity, or delegation depth.
Authorization use requires a fresh proof of possession that was not supplied.
The registered native proof profile did not validate possession of the subject key.
A persona-issued authorization is not reachable from authoritative canonical repository state.
Concurrent non-monotonic claim-ledger state remains unresolved and cannot authorize.
The claim's bounded validity interval has ended.
An irreversible valid revocation covers the claim.
The signer is not permitted to revoke this authorization or descriptive assertion.
A device lacks an active durable NID-bearing claim-ledger-reader authorization.
Presented claim-ledger state regresses below a previously finalized checkpoint.
The minting node lacks active oidc-token-issuer authority for the persona.
The minting node cannot decrypt or use an active shared issuer signing key.
The authoritative ledger checkpoint exceeds the issuer manifest's at-most-300-second freshness bound.
The requesting OAuth/OIDC client is not explicitly registered.
The request uses Client Credentials, implicit, password, or another prohibited grant.
The requested claim release lacks the required persona consent.
Requested claims exceed the intersection of scope, audience, policy, consent, trust, and active state.
Discovery metadata, JWT iss, or continuity state names a different exact issuer URL.
A JWT is missing or misuses the token-type separation required by the profile.
The JWT audience does not authorize the relying party or protected resource.
The pinned draft-21 Status List Token is expired, outside ttl, or not fresh enough for policy.
The HTTPS and Radicle status copies are not byte-identical under the continuity digest.
A status index is out of range, reused, or outside its writer-NID namespace allocation.
The token status is INVALID or cannot provide valid evidence of VALID.

security_invariants.description: The cold-root npub and accepted KEL are authoritative for persona identity; downstream caches and delegated identifiers cannot override them.
A Radicle NID delegation is active only after both the persona epoch-key BIP-340 signature and the delegated NID Ed25519 proof verify over the same binding.
Every signed object is locally signature-verified and, where applicable, delegation-checked before rendering, storage, or authorization.
Core discovery does not depend on a centralized persona, npub, RID, or serving-node directory.
Persona nsec, NID secrets, and sensitive cached identity material are protected by the Core keys-repository profile, including NIP-49 wrapping where applicable.
Tier 3 content is audience-key encrypted before reaching any repository, seed, full node, or relay.
Tier 2 private repositories are selective-replication boundaries, not encryption, and clients present that trust boundary honestly.
Comms-owned non-key private state and audience or ratchet material are encrypted under the Comms repository-encryption profile.
Cross-backend Comms processing runs on user-controlled clients; full nodes, repository relays, routing nodes, and Nostr relays are blind carriers for protected plaintext.
Feed, outbox, and delivery discovery do not depend on a centralized delivery directory.
Private Matrix discussion and configuration content, including protected state, remains end-to-end encrypted and downgrade-resistant from the homeserver.
A Matrix MXID delegation requires both the persona epoch-key signature and successful MXID self-publication through Matrix state authorization.
Private mute, feed-preference, followed-repository, and other Social state are encrypted at rest using the owning Social or bound Comms profile.
Matrix and cross-protocol Social bridging runs on user-controlled clients; no homeserver or relay bridge receives protected plaintext.
Following, transitive discovery, and social-graph evaluation do not depend on a centralized follow-graph oracle.
Control audit records containing requests, grants, tokens, or side effects are encrypted at rest under Core, Comms, and Control-owned protection rules without a Social dependency.
A Control session device never receives persona epoch, NID, audience, repository-decryption, or ratchet secrets.
Claim IDs, event signatures, issuer authority, typed references, and native proofs are verified before trust or authorization policy is applied.
Every delegated claim strictly preserves or narrows all authority dimensions and issuance chains contain at most eight edges.
Persona-issued device authorization is final only in canonical private claim-repository state, while authenticated reductions take effect immediately.
A valid revocation or authority reduction is irreversible, monotonic, and wins concurrent repository merges.
Private claim-ledger contents and decryption material are available only to active durable NID-bearing ledger readers.
Shared OIDC signing keys are separately encrypted and released only to nodes with active oidc-token-issuer authority.
A node mints only from a synchronized canonical checkpoint no older than the manifest bound, which cannot exceed 300 seconds.
HTTPS issuer metadata and the root-key-scoped Radicle continuity tree agree on the exact active issuer, keys, status digests, and authorized succession.
OIDC projection releases only claims allowed by scope, audience, client policy, consent, active repository state, issuer trust, and proof requirements.
JWT consumers enforce exact issuer, intended audience, time, signature, nonce when applicable, and token-type separation including typ at+jwt for access tokens.
Draft-21 status lists are signed, fresh, digest-bound across HTTPS and Radicle mirrors, writer-namespaced without index reuse, and never let VALID override other token failures.
